content.title: About
content.content: Cod (Gadus morhua) is a marine fish from the cod family that lives in cold northern Atlantic waters. Its flesh is white, flaky, and mildly flavored, rich in protein and low in fat. Cod is commonly baked, broiled, or grilled, and is also used in soups and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod is one of the world’s most important commercial fish species, with annual catches exceeding 5 million tonnes.
Wild cod can grow over 2 m long and weigh more than 100 kg, though most market fish are much smaller.
Cod contains low levels of mercury, making it a safe choice for frequent consumption.
The fish can change its skin coloration to blend with its surroundings, helping it avoid predators.
Cod is the primary ingredient in many fish sticks and processed fish fillets.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 18 g of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Cod is low in saturated fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: While lower than fatty fish, cod still supplies EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in vitamin B12, niacin (B3), and B6, which aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bone strength.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cod.

items.title: Contamination
items.content: Occasionally cod can contain trace amounts of heavy metals or microplastics; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large portions may cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cod can be baked with herbs and lemon, broiled on a grill, steamed, or added to soups. Fillets are easy to portion, marinate, or bread. Pair with vegetables, potatoes, or whole grains for a balanced meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cod in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic, and use within 2 days. Frozen cod should be stored at –18 °C and consumed within 3‑4 months. Before cooking, check for a mild sea scent; discard if it smells strong or ammonia‑like.
